newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia AWB says held no wheat talks with India.
newsitem.headline: Australia AWB says held no wheat talks with India.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Thursday it had held no discussions with India over the possibility India might sell one million tonnes of wheat it has contracted to buy from Australia to other countries.
"At this stage it has not been discussed with us and certainly that is something we would not be entertaining," Tim Dewan, an official of the AWB's international division told Reuters.
"If we sell to India, it is destination India," Dewan added.
The Indian agriculture minister on Wednesday said India might sell one million tonnes of wheat from Australia to other countries if trade "behaves normally."

"If the trade behaves normally, we may divert it, but if there is hoarding, we will use that wheat to control the domestic prices," Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra told a press conference in New Delhi.

Since December, India has contracted to import 2.3 million tonnes of wheat from Australia, out of which 1.3 million tonnes has arrived. Shipments of the remaining one million tonnes is due after July.
Weed seeds were detected in the initial Australian shipments but Mishra said it was not harmful and was common in wheat of any origin.
Dewan said that normally wheat is consumed by the country that purchases it.
Dewan said he was under the impression India was short on wheat and therefore unlikely to "on-sell" any of the wheat it has contracted to buy.
"If they need wheat to maintain the procurement for the PDS (public distribution system) they are also short," Dewan said.
Dewan also said Australia would consider selling more wheat to India, although the AWB's position was currently very tight.
"But for the 1997/98 crop, we would certainly look at it," he said.
